cases.question: What happens if a team uses an Aggregated Standard Traded Player Exception in a trade that would put Apron Team Salary over the Second Apron Level?

claims.text: The Transaction Restrictions Table assigns the Second Apron Level as the Applicable Apron Level for a team acquiring a player using an Aggregated Standard Traded Player Exception (row H).
claims.quote: H. Team acquires a player using an Aggregated Standard Traded Player Exception (as described in Section 6(j)(1)(ii) below) Second Apron Level

claims.text: The CBA's own worked example confirms the result: a proposed trade using the Aggregated Standard Traded Player Exception that would leave the team's Apron Team Salary above the Second Apron Level is prohibited.
claims.quote: The proposed trade (a transaction set forth in row H of the Transaction Restrictions Table with an Applicable Apron Level of the Second Apron Level) is prohibited by Section 2(e)(2)(i)(A) above because, immediately following the trade, Team D’s 2024-25 Apron Team Salary would exceed $189.5 million (i.e., the 2024-25 Second Apron Level).

claims.text: In addition, a team that does engage in such a transaction may not, for the remainder of that Salary Cap Year, have an Apron Team Salary exceeding the Second Apron Level.
claims.quote: A Team that engages in a transaction set forth in the Transaction Restrictions Table may not, for the remainder of such Salary Cap Year, have an Apron Team Salary that exceeds the Applicable Apron Level that corresponds with such transaction in the table.

cases.question: When is a player still eligible for NBA Most Valuable Player if he did not play sixty-five Regular Season games?

claims.text: A player who did not play 65 Regular Season games is still eligible for NBA Most Valuable Player if he (A) played in at least 62 Regular Season games, (B) suffered a "season-ending injury," and (C) played in at least 85% of the Regular Season games played by his Team prior to suffering that injury.
claims.quote:
(2) the player (A) played in at least sixty -two (62) Regular Season games, 
(B) suffered a “season-ending injury” (as defined below), and (C) played in 
at least eighty-five percent (85%) of the Regular Season games played by his 
Team prior to the player suffering such injury.

claims.text: A "season-ending injury" for this purpose is an injury that, in the opinion of a physician jointly selected by the NBA and Players Association, makes it substantially more likely than not that the player would be unable to play through the May 31 following the date of the injury.
claims.quote:
(A) A “season -ending injury” is an injury that, in the 
opinion of a physician jointly selected by the NBA 
and Players Association, makes it substantially more 
likely than not that the player would be unable to 
play through the May 31 following the date of such 
injury

claims.text: Separately, a player who fails to satisfy the Award Eligibility Criteria in a Season may still be deemed eligible for MVP if he prevails in either an Award Eligibility Grievance or an Extraordinary Circumstances Challenge for that Season (though he may not bring both for the same Season).
claims.quote:
(ii) A player who fails to satisfy the Award Eligibility Criteria in 
a Season may nonetheless be deemed eligible for the 
Applicable Generally Recognized League Honors if he 
prevails in either an Award Eligibility Grievance or an 
Extraordinary Circumstances Challenge in respect of such 
Season in accordance with the procedures set forth in 
Sections 6(b) and 6(c) below.  A player may not bring both 
an Award Eligibility Grievance and an Extraordinary 
Circumstances Challenge in respect of the same Season.

claims.text: To prevail in an Award Eligibility Grievance, the player must prove by clear and convincing evidence that the Team willfully limited his minutes played or games played during the Regular Season with the intention of depriving him of eligibility for honors such as MVP; the sole remedy is that he is deemed eligible.
claims.quote:
To prevail in an Award Eligibility Grievance in respect of a 
Season, the player bears the burden of proving, by clear and 
convincing evidence, that the Team willfully limited the 
player’s number of minutes played or games played during 
the Regular Season with the intention of depriving the player 
of eligibility for one or more of the Applicable Generally 
Recognized League Honors for such Season.

claims.text: To prevail in an Extraordinary Circumstances Challenge, the player must prove that extraordinary circumstances made it impracticable for him to play in one or more of the Regular Season games he missed, that he would have satisfied the 65-game criterion had he played every game missed due to those circumstances (assuming 20 minutes in each such missed game), and that, taking into account the totality of the circumstances, it would be unjust to exclude him from eligibility.
claims.quote:
(A) Due to extraordinary circumstances, it was  
impracticable for him to play in one (1) or more of 
the Regular Season game(s) that he missed during 
such Season; 
(B) He wo uld have satisfied the Award Eligibility 
Criterion set forth in Section 6(a)(1) above if he had 
played in every game that he missed due to the 
extraordinary circumstances ( i.e., assuming that he 
would have played twenty (20) minutes in each such 
missed game); and  
(C) As a result of the extraordinary circumstances, and 
taking into account the totality of the circumstances, 
including whether the player did not play in other 
Regular Season games in which he could have played 
during such Season, it would be unjust to exclude the 
player from eligibility for the Applicable Generally 
Recognized League Honors for such Season.

cases.question: How does the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception change above the Second Apron Level, and which transaction table covers that limit?

claims.text: The Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception is governed by the Transaction Restrictions Table in Section 2(e)(4) — the table referenced as "the transactions listed in the table in Section 2(e)(4) below (the 'Transaction Restrictions Table')".
claims.quote:
shall apply with respect to the transactions listed in the table 
in Section 2(e)(4) below (the “Transaction Restrictions 
Table”):

claims.text: In that table, the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception appears as row K, and its Applicable Apron Level is the Second Apron Level: "K. Team signs a player using the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception (as described in Section 6(f) below)" — Second Apron Level.
claims.quote:
K. Team signs a player using the Taxpayer 
Mid-Level Salary Exception (as described in  
Section 6(f) below) 
Second Apron 
Level

claims.text: The Second Apron Level limit operates as a hard ceiling tied to that row: a team may not sign a player using the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception if, immediately following the signing, its Apron Team Salary would exceed the Second Apron Level, and it may not exceed that level for the remainder of the Salary Cap Year. The CBA's own example confirms this: a 2025-26 signing under the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception is "a transaction set forth in row K of the Transaction Restrictions Table with an Applicable Apron of the Second Apron Level," permitted only because the team's Apron Team Salary of $195 million was less than or equal to the $199 million Second Apron Level, after which the team may not have an Apron Team Salary exceeding $199 million for the remainder of that Salary Cap Year.
claims.quote:
Such signing (a transaction set forth in row K of the Transaction Restrictions 
Table with an Applicable Apron of the Second Apron Level )

claims.text: The general rule that enforces the table's Apron Level is Section 2(e)(2)(i): a team may not engage in a listed transaction if, immediately following it, the team's Apron Team Salary would exceed the Applicable Apron Level corresponding to that transaction, and it may not exceed that level for the remainder of the Salary Cap Year.
claims.quote:
(A) A Team may not engage in a transaction set forth in the 
Transaction Restrictions Table if, immediately following such 
transaction, the Team’s Apron Team Salary for such Salary Cap 
Year would exceed the “Applicable Apron Level ” that corresponds with 
such transaction in the table; and

claims.text: Using the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception also triggers additional transaction restrictions: for each Salary Cap Year beginning with 2024-25, a team that has signed a contract under the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception may not engage in any transaction in rows A through F of the Transaction Restrictions Table (for 2023-24 the cutoff was rows A through E).
claims.quote:
(B) For ea ch Salary Cap Year beginning with the 
2024-25 Salary Cap Year, a Team may not engage in 
any transaction set forth in rows A through F of the 
Transaction Restrictions Table  if it has previously 
signed a Player Contract pursuant to the Taxpayer 
Mid-Level Salary Exception during such Salary Cap 
Year.

claims.text: The exception itself is only available to a team whose Apron Team Salary immediately after using it exceeds the First Apron Level, so the Second Apron Level in row K is the upper bound of the band in which the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception may be used.
claims.quote:
provided that the Team’s 
Apron Team Salary immediately following the Team’s use of such 
Exception exceeds the First Apron Level

cases.question: What counts toward the cap as Salary, and how is Team Salary determined?

claims.text: In computing Team Salary, the Agreement requires inclusion of the aggregate Salaries of all active players (and former players to the extent the Agreement provides) attributable to a particular Salary Cap Year, along with the other listed amounts.
claims.quote: (a) Computation. For purposes of computing Team Salary under this Agreement, all of the following amounts shall be included: (1) Subject to the rules set forth in this Article VII, the aggregate Salaries of all active players (and former players to the extent provided by the terms of this Agreement) attributable to a particular Salary Cap Year

claims.text: Performance Bonuses count toward Salary only if they would be earned assuming the Team’s or player’s performance were identical to the prior Salary Cap Year’s performance (subject to the challenge procedures in Sections 3(d)(2)-(4)).
claims.quote: any Performance Bonus (provided such Performance Bonus may be included in a Player Contract in accordance with Section 5(b) below), shall be included in Salary only if such Performance Bonus would be earned if the Team’s or player’s performance were identical to the performance in the immediately preceding Salary Cap Year.

claims.text: All Incentive Compensation described in Article II, Sections 3(b)(iii) and 3(c) is included in Salary.
claims.quote: All Incentive Compensation described in Article II, Sections 3(b)(iii) and 3(c) shall be included in Salary.

cases.question: An Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agent has a prior regular salary of 10000000 and the prior average player salary is 12000000. What is the first-year cap under the veteran free agent exception?

claims.text: Under the Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agent exception, the first-year cap is the greater of 175% of prior Regular Salary (plus applicable bonuses) or 105% of the prior Average Player Salary. With prior Regular Salary of $10,000,000 and no bonuses given: 175% × $10,000,000 = $17,500,000; 105% × $12,000,000 = $12,600,000. The greater amount is $17,500,000.
claims.quote: (A) one hundred seventy-five percent (175%) of the Regular Salary for the final Salary Cap Year covered by his prior Contract, plus one hundred seventy-five percent (175%) of any Likely Bonuses and Unlikely Bonuses, respectively, called for in the final Salary Cap Year covered by the player’s prior Contract, or (B) Salary plus Unlikely Bonuses totaling an amount equal to one hundred five percent (105%) of the Average Player Salary for the prior Salary Cap Year

cases.question: What does Salary include, and does it include Unlikely Bonuses?

claims.text: Salary is defined, for a Salary Cap Year, as the player's Compensation with respect to the Season covered by that Salary Cap Year, plus any other amount deemed to constitute Salary under the Agreement, plus any consideration received by a retired player that is deemed Salary under Article XIII.
claims.quote:
(lll) “Salary” means, with respect to a Salary Cap Year, a player’s 
Compensation with respect to the Season covered by such Salary Cap Year, 
plus any other amount that is deemed to constitute Salary in accordance with 
the terms of this Agreement

claims.text: Salary does not include Unlikely Bonuses; the definition expressly excludes Unlikely Bonuses, along with benefits received under the Agreement (e.g., Article IV benefits, per diem, moving expenses) and any portion of Compensation attributable to another Salary Cap Year.
claims.quote:
not including Unlikely Bonuses, any benefits 
the player received in accordanc e with the terms of this Agreement 
(including, e.g., the benefits provided for by Article IV, per diem, and moving 
expenses), and any portion of the player’s Compensation that is attributable 
to another Salary Cap Year in accordance with this Agreement.

claims.text: Salary also includes any consideration received by a retired player that is deemed to constitute Salary in accordance with Article XIII.
claims.quote:
S alary also 
includes any consideration received by a retired player that is deemed to 
constitute Salary in accordance with the terms of Article XIII.

cases.question: How many seasons can a contract signed with the mid-level exception run for a team that is over the Salary Cap?

response.message: More than one retrieved passage applies, and none says which one controls. Which season or effective date do you mean?

claims.text: Under the Non-Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception — one of the mid-level exceptions available to a team at or above the Salary Cap — a signed contract may run no more than four (4) Seasons.
claims.quote:
(2) The term of a Player Contract signed pursuant to the 
Non-Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception may not exceed four (4) 
Seasons in length, and the remaining term of a Player Contract 
acquired by assignment pursuant to the Non- Taxpayer Mid-Level 
Salary Exception may not exceed four (4) Seasons in length.

claims.text: Under the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception — the other mid-level exception, used where the team's Apron Team Salary exceeds the First Apron Level — a signed contract may not exceed two (2) Seasons in length.

sign one (1) or more Player Contracts during each Salary Cap Year 
not to exceed two (2) Seasons in length

cases.question: What can't a second-apron team do in a trade?

claims.text: A Second Apron Team is prohibited from trading (conditionally or unconditionally) its first round draft pick in the first NBA Draft that occurs following the seventh Season that follows the Season occurring within such Salary Cap Year.
claims.quote:
(i) the Team shall be prohibited from trading (either 
conditionally or unconditionally) its first round draft pick in 
the first NBA Draft that occurs following the seventh 
Season that follows the Season occurring within such Salary 
Cap Year; and

claims.text: Even after that restriction runs, the pick can still be subject to a Draft Pick Penalty: with respect to the four Salary Cap Years immediately following such Salary Cap Year, if the Team is a Second Apron Team for two or more of those four Salary Cap Years, the first round draft pick is subject to a Draft Pick Penalty (it becomes the final pick in the first round).
claims.quote:
(A) If the Team is a Second Apron Team for two (2) or 
more of such four (4) Salary Cap Years, then such 
first round draft pick shall be subject to a Draft Pick 
Penalty; and

claims.text: The rule applies to a "Second Apron Team," defined for a Salary Cap Year as a Team that, as of the start of the Team's last Regular Season game occurring within such Salary Cap Year, has an Apron Team Salary exceeding the Second Apron Level for that Salary Cap Year; the salary-cap prohibitions in this Section apply beginning with the 2024-25 Salary Cap Year.
claims.quote:
“Second Apron Team” means, for a Salary Cap Year, a Team 
that, as of the start of the Team’s last Regular Season game 
occurring within such Salary Cap Year, has an Apron Team 
Salary for such Salary Cap Year that exceeds the Second 
Apron Level for such Salary Cap Year.
